title: Overfitting
text: Overfitting happens when a model memorizes training data and fails on new data. Regularization, dropout, early stopping and more data reduce it.

title: Cross-validation
text: K-fold cross-validation splits data into k parts, training on k-1 and validating on the rest, giving a more reliable estimate of generalization.

title: Gradient descent
text: Gradient descent iteratively updates parameters in the direction that reduces the loss function, controlled by a learning rate.

title: Random forest
text: A random forest averages many decision trees trained on bootstrapped samples and random feature subsets to reduce variance.

title: Precision and recall
text: Precision is the share of predicted positives that are correct; recall is the share of actual positives found. F1 balances both.

title: Feature scaling
text: Standardization and min-max scaling put features on comparable ranges, which helps distance-based and gradient-based models.

title: Class imbalance
text: When one class is rare, use resampling, class weights, or metrics like PR-AUC instead of plain accuracy.

title: SQL joins
text: INNER JOIN keeps matching rows, LEFT JOIN keeps all left rows plus matches, and FULL JOIN keeps rows from both sides.

title: Window functions
text: SQL window functions like ROW_NUMBER, RANK and LAG compute values across related rows without collapsing them.

title: Data cleaning
text: Cleaning means handling missing values, removing duplicates, fixing types and treating outliers before analysis.

title: Dashboards
text: Good Power BI or Tableau dashboards lead with key KPIs, use consistent colors, and let users filter by time and segment.

title: A/B testing
text: An A/B test compares two variants on a metric, using a significance test to check the difference is not random noise.

title: REST APIs with FastAPI
text: FastAPI builds typed REST APIs in Python with automatic validation and interactive OpenAPI documentation.

title: Caching
text: Caching stores frequent results in memory, for example Redis, to cut latency and database load.

title: Docker
text: Docker packages an application with its dependencies into a container that runs the same on any machine.

title: Database indexing
text: An index speeds up reads by avoiding full table scans, at the cost of slower writes and extra storage.

title: Vector databases
text: A vector database stores embeddings and finds nearest neighbours quickly, enabling semantic search and recommendations.

title: Retrieval-augmented generation
text: RAG retrieves relevant documents and passes them to a language model so answers are grounded in real data.

title: Embeddings
text: Embeddings map text to dense vectors so that texts with similar meaning end up close together.

title: HNSW index
text: HNSW is a layered graph structure for approximate nearest neighbour search, trading a little recall for large speedups.

title: Chunking
text: Splitting long documents into overlapping chunks keeps each embedding focused and improves retrieval quality.

title: Prompt engineering
text: Clear instructions, examples and output formats help language models give consistent, useful responses.
